messages:
mira: Heads-up — after today's canary for nova-rlhf-4b (4-bit quant, v2) were seeing high repetition and rerank decay on long prompts. Support flagged several customer repros. :eyes:
deploy-bot: rollout: nova-rlhf-4b:v2 deployed to dedicated-canary (10% traffic) at 1968000000.
jonathan: Can you paste a minimal sample?
mira: Sample from the customer: "System: write a long spec. User: ..." output has a repeating section: "the system will the system will the system will" — repeats start ~token 220.
sara: That smells like KV-cache / cache alignment + quant kernel change. We saw similar with fused-attn switch last quarter.
ryan: Quick metrics: comparing pre-rollout -> post-rollout (canary) on long-context evals: ngram-repeat-3 rate jumped from 3.1% -> 6.8%. Avg token-latency +8%.
jonathan: Which runtime flags changed in v2?
mira: Two changes: 1) 4-bit qlora checkpoint, 2) enable fused-attn-optimized kernel (flag: --fused-attn=true).
jonathan: First quick experiment: can we repro with same checkpoint but --fused-attn=false? If repeat goes away, kernel is suspect. Command: 
```
redwoodctl serve --model nova-rlhf-4b:v2 --quant=4bit --fused-attn=false --canary=local
```
sara: On it. Spinning a local canary run now. Will run eval-suite/regression-longcontext and collect failing prompts.
ops-bot: eval-run started: eval-suite/regression-longcontext -> run-id=evr_1968000123
jonathan: Also try flushing KV-cache between segments — there was a bug where cache-offsets were computed using 32-bit offsets but quant path used 16-bit in v2. Might cause misaligned reads.
ryan: I dumped token embeddings before/after quant path for one failing prompt — small offsets mismatch visible in bytes 128-136. Posting snippet below:
```
# hex dump (trimmed)
pre-quant: ... 7a 3b 9c ...
post-quant: ... 7a 3b 1c ...
```
mira: If it's an offset bug we'll need a hotfix. For now I'm pausing the canary and rolling back to v1 on canary pool.
deploy-bot: canary paused by mira at 1968000245. rollback to nova-rlhf-4b:v1 initiated.
sara: Local repro with --fused-attn=false reduces ngram-repeat to 3.4% (close to baseline). So kernel looks suspicious.
jonathan: Good isolate. Next steps: 1) create a short regression test that catches this (long-context repeat), 2) bisect fused-attn changes in runtime, 3) run full eval-suite against v2 kernel+v1 rounding code, 4) keep canary paused until fix.
mira: I'll file a P0 github issue with failing prompts + eval links and assign to @jonathan + @sara. Also notify infra for a hotfix release cadence.
ryan: Adding perf notes: one hypothesis is that fused kernel changed memory layout that interacts poorly with our 4-bit packing. Might explain both latency and repeats.
jonathan: I'll start a bisect: runtime commits around fused-attn merge (range c3f2..d9a0). If urgent we can revert the fused kernel flag cluster.
ops-bot: issue created: GH#12345 "nova-rlhf-4b:v2 repetition after fused-attn" assigned to jonathan, sara.
mira: Thanks — owners noted. Can we set an eval alert to email on ngram-repeat >5% for a week after fix? Want to monitor regression window.
sara: Will add alert rule and a regression dashboard panel.
ryan: I'll keep collecting failing customer context and add to the reproducibility pack.
jonathan: Plan: bisect today, propose PR with either kernel fix or revert flag. If we revert we should keep quant v2 checkpoint but serve with fused-attn=false until verified.
mira: Agreed. Leaving canary paused. I'll update the incident thread after PR. :thumbsup:
